questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from his test results?

questions.answerText: There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues. 血液化验结果是清白的（没问题）。没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 医生宣布结果的直接陈述句。医生一坐下就直接通报结论 The blood test came back clear 并补一句 There is no indication of any digestive issues——这种“医生直接公布检查结 果”的陈述就是答案信号，不用等转折。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: no indication of any digestive issues ↔nothing wrong with his digestive system “没有消化问题迹象”=“消化系统没毛病”

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: C) 原词陷阱 录音查的是 blood test 与 digestive issues，an issue with his blood circulation 借用了 “血液 blood”的耳熟感，却把对象偷换成 blood circulation（血液循环），录音从未说循环 有问题，且结果是 clear（清白），与“有问题”正好相反。 借用原文：The blood test came back clear A) 过度推断 录音只说某项检查没问题，It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life 却推到 “可望享有健康人生”——录音里他正feel poorly、被诊断有压力，谈不上健康一生，是无中 生有的拔高。 D) 答非所问 He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health 套用了后文“压力潜伏二 十年而不自知”的影子，但本题问的是 test results（化验结果），结果恰恰是“清白”，并未 说明他长期体弱，错位安插。 借用原文：You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it

questions.stem: What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?

questions.answerText: Being unaware of the stress they are under.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. 你刚才描述的是一种很常见的心态。许多承受压力的人都意识不到自己有压力。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 含 common / Many people 的概括句。女方用 a common sentiment 与 Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it 对“很多人”下普遍性判断——出现 common、 Many people 这类总括词，就是“普遍现象”题的答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it ↔ Being unaware of the stress they are under “承压却没认出”=“没意识到自己身处压力”

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: D) 偷换概念 Suffering from illness without recognising it 与答案句框架一致（都是“X 而不自知”）， 但 X 被换成 illness；录音说的是 suffer from stress fail to recognise it——没认出的是压 力不是疾病，差的正是那个核心变量。 借用原文：Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it A) 与原文相反 Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress 是“把病当成压力”，而录音是“有压力却没认出 （把压力当别的）”，方向恰好反过来；男方原话是 I've never felt stress，是不承认压力， 不是错把病当压力。 B) 原词陷阱 Complaining they are being overworked 蹭了录音 overwork and stress 的 overwork，但女方说的是很多人“没意识到压力”，恰恰不是“抱怨过劳”；男方甚至说 other people complain，他自己不抱怨，与“很多人抱怨”相反。 借用原文：It's probably due to overwork and stress

questions.stemZh: 男士对他所从事的行业说了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. 我是个餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: this industry is very + 形容词的直接评价句。男方自陈身份后用 this industry is very competitive 直接评价所在行业——this industry is very + 形容词的结构就是“行业评价” 题的答案信号，落点在 competitive 这个词。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: this industry is very competitive ↔It is full of competition “非常有竞争性”=“充满竞争”

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 It calls for responsible management 蹭了男方自报身份 I'm a restaurant manager 里的 manager/management，但他评价行业用的词是 competitive，从没说这行“需要负责任的 管理”，是借身份词造的干扰。 借用原文：I'm a restaurant manager B) 未提及 It proves to be quite profitable 谈盈利，但男方对行业的描述只有“竞争激烈”和“事务繁 多”，从未提到赚钱与否，是无中生有。 C) 未提及 It is remarkably promising 说行业前景可观，但录音里男方谈的是竞争和繁忙、并被建议 放慢节奏，全无“前景大好”之意，属凭空添加的正面评价。 1 W: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams. The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player. John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25. Why did you retire so early? W: 今天《新闻人物》的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。这个名字你可能不太熟悉,但约翰曾经是一位备受赞誉的篮 球运动员。约翰,你在25岁时离开体坛让球迷们感到震惊。你为什么这么早就退役了? 2 M: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention. M: Meg,我热爱做运动员,但我不喜欢当名人。我还在上高中时就成了焦点人物,高中毕业后就直接转职业 了,这是个错误。我是个害羞的孩子,还没准备好面对所有媒体的关注。 3 W: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary. When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury. W: 但是在职业生涯巅峰时期放弃数百万美元,大多数人都无法抵挡这么高薪水的诱惑。当你离开体坛时,有 人猜测你和队友有矛盾,甚至有伤病。 4 M: Not at all. It was hard to quit. I was tempted to stay in the game, because I love basketball and I loved my team. As for money, I turned professional at 18. So I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisers. I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young. M: 完全不是。退出很难。我很想留在赛场上,因为我热爱篮球,也爱我的球队。至于钱,我18岁就转职业 了。所以实际上我已经赚了很多钱,而且大部分都存起来了,因为我有很棒的财务顾问。我知道对大多数球 员来说篮球不是一个能干很久的职业,所以我想趁还年轻的时候转行。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 W: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. Why? W: 好的,那是20年前的事了,现在你又上新闻了。你创建了一个基金会,致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。 为什么? 6 M: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. The foundation is just the latest attempt. M: 我上了大学,学习公共卫生,了解到肥胖流行病的严重性,特别是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年中。过去二十 年我一直在努力缓解这个问题。这个基金会只是最新的尝试。 7 W: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right? W: 基金会用私人捐款来支持小学女孩和男孩的篮球队,对吧? 8 M: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too, and also have some public funding. M: 实际上,我们也支持中学生的球队,而且还有一些公共资金。

analysis.text: spent...trying 与题干同款行动句。原文 I\'ve spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem 与题干 spent the last two decades trying to do 几乎逐词对应， 是直接锁定答案的持续行动句。

analysis.text: trying to alleviate the problem ↔Alleviate the obesity problem. 缓解这个问题=缓解肥胖问题

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 借用原文 I studied public health，但研究公共健康是他在大学里的学习，是认识问题的 前提，而非他二十年来「致力做」的那件事；真正的长期目标是缓解肥胖。 借用原文：I studied public health C) 原词陷阱 C 借用原文 also have some public funding 里的 public funding，但那只是基金会的资 金来源之一，原文并未说他二十年来一直在筹集足够的公共资金，属错置内容。 借用原文：also have some public funding D) 偷换概念 D 借用篮球相关词，原文确有 basketball teams 与让孩子打球，但那是缓解肥胖的手段， 且对象是普通中小学生而非培养 young basketball players，目的被偷换。 借用原文：support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school Section B 1 Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951. She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author. She studied English Literature at University in Scotland. After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature. Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981. She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award. The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV. She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh—the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000. Kate Atkinson 于1951年出生于英格兰约克郡。她努力获得了作为作家的资历。她在苏格兰的大学学习英 国文学。1974年毕业后,她研究了美国文学博士学位。后来,她在毕业的大学任教,并于1981年开始写短篇 小说。1986年赢得Woman's Own短篇小说大赛后,她开始为女性杂志撰稿。她的第一部小说《博物馆幕 后》赢得了1995年英国年度图书奖。这本书以约克郡为背景,已被改编为广播剧、舞台剧和电视剧。她为 爱丁堡的一家剧院创作了两部戏剧——第一部名为《Nice》,第二部是《Abandonment》,于2000年8月 作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。 2 Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor. Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized. Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners. Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception. 什么是真正的创造者?创造者是从无到有创造出某物的天才吗?不是。创造者只是使用他们所继承的东西的 人类,他们吸收过去并操纵它来创造可能的未来。因此,人类作为创造者是常态而非例外。

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项 It seeks inspiration for novel inventions 拼用了原文 inspiration 和 one invention enables or inspires further inventions 里的词；但讲者明说新想法"几乎像魔法般灵感闪 现"只是大众误解，他真正主张的是"靠先例"，故"四处寻找灵感"并非讲者的机制描述。 借用原文：They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few B) 偷换概念 选项 constantly absorbs new information 听上去像"大脑怎么运作"的合理答案，且 absorb 一词原文第五段确实念到 absorb the past；但原文说的是"吸收过去/旧的东西"， 选项偷换成"不断吸收新信息"，方向正好相反，差在 past 被改成 new information。 借用原文：absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures D) 与原文相反 选项 repeats precedent on a regular basis 借走了原文 works from precedent 的 precedent；但讲者说的是"依凭先例去拼出新东西"，强调的是"造新"，选项却说成"只是定 期重复先例"，把创造性的"用旧造新"歪曲为机械重复，与原意相反。 借用原文：The human brain works from precedent 1 Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time. Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions. This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change. If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans. 许多狗主人会告诉你,他们的狗不知怎的就能知道他们生病或心烦意乱,而根据研究狗认知的研究人员的说 法,这些宠物主人是对的。狗确实知道它们的人类同伴正在经历艰难时刻。你的狗不仅能感知到你感冒了, 而且家犬已经表现出能够察觉到更细微的情绪波动和更严重的身体状况的能力。这是因为狗对它们熟悉的 人的变化极其敏感,而疾病会引起变化。例如,如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌,他们的气味就会异常,而狗能够 闻到这种变化,即使人类闻不到,因为狗的嗅觉比人类要强大得多。 2 Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell. Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well. Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes. 研究人员还发现,一个人的情绪——它可能是更大疾病的指示器——会触发狗的嗅觉。人类情绪在身体散 发的化学信号中物理显现,而狗也能够闻到这些信号。除了嗅觉,狗还从人的声音中收集信息以感知变化。 3 In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone. A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness. What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes. Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear. What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation. 2014年,研究人员发现狗的大脑中有一个与人类相似的区域,使它们能够理解说话者声音语调中的情感暗示, 这超出了它们仅从熟悉的词语中能够获取的信息。人的声音也能携带疾病的指示信号。目前还不太清楚的 是狗对这些变化理解到什么程度。人类发出大量的暗示,但狗是否知道其中一些暗示意味着疾病并不清楚。 我们认为是狗表现出的关心,可能更像是增加的好奇心或怀疑我们出了什么问题,而紧紧跟随是收集更多关 于这种情况信息的好方法。 4 Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer. But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future. For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases. 一些研究人员断言狗有朝一日会帮助医生诊断疾病,因为一些狗已经展示出能够检测各种疾病的能力,包括 糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。但这些研究人员承认这可能是在遥远的将来。目前,研究表明养狗本身就可以带 来一系列好处。养宠物狗已被证明能增强健康和提升情绪。狗还能帮助人们放松,而且对于那些患有慢性疾 病的人来说,它们可以是一种特别的慰藉。

analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 ensure owners suffer fewer chronic diseases 借了录音的 chronic diseases，但原文说 狗能给"患慢病者"以慰藉 a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases，不是说 养狗能"减少患慢病"，方向被偷换，且 ensure 也过强。 借用原文：they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases C) 原词陷阱 reduce owners' risk of getting cancer or diabetes 借了录音 diabetes and certain types of cancer，但那是讲狗"诊断"疾病、且明说在 distant future，并非 for now 的结 论；题问 for now，C 取错了时间段。 借用原文：detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer D) 未提及 alert owners to the seriousness of their conditions（提醒病情有多严重）录音从未说 过；末段讲的是养狗"增进健康、提振心情、给予慰藉"，没有"警示病情严重程度"一说。 1 Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money. Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored. 本月早些时候,名为Onward的智库发布了一份报告《学位问题》,该报告认为创意艺术学位不具备良好的性 价比。据Onward称,部长们应该"打击那些在毕业十年后为学生提供极其有限价值的课程",限制此类课程招 Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. 收新生的能力,如果毕业生平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛的话。应该优先支持科学、技术、工程、数学和 经济学等毕业生平均收入较高的课程。 2 The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money. At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, ten years after graduation. Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students—have fairly good work prospects. Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents. The rewards that education gives us are not measurable. They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct. Consumption drives the American economy ↔ultimately boosts the nation's economy A 项用 ultimately 把 P8 的两句话压成一句因果，与预判的"加薪 消费 经济增长"完 全一致。 B) 偷换概念 He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. 是福特出于产能目的支付溢价；The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. 中"工人变顾客"是意外结果， 并非"支付溢价"直接导向"吸引更多顾客"。 C) 与原文相反 原文 workers who are paid more can spend more 是高工资 高消费，选项反成"消 费刺激加薪欲望"，因果链方向倒置。 D) 过度推断 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness.—— 作者只是说"暂且搁置"公平这一旧论据，并未说它过时。 根据传统观念,提高工资的依据是什么? A) 分配的公平性。 B) 生产率的提高。 C) 经济政策制定者的优先事项。 D) 市场力量的准确判断。

options.label: A
options.text: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.stem: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom? 用 What 直问按传统观点加薪的依据，回原文找明确陈述句。 49. What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom? A) Fairness in distribution. B) Increase in productivity. C) The priority of economic policymakers. D) The unerring judgment of market forces.

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主句 What is the basis for higher wages + 介词短语 according to the conventional wisdom——according to 引出陈述主体，意味着答案要看 conventional wisdom 那方怎 么说，而非作者本人怎么说；六级常借这个介词短语区分立场，须警觉。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. 中"公平"是作者列出的另一种加薪理由（且被搁置），与 conventional wisdom 无关。 B) ✓ 正确 productivity growth ↔Increase in productivity. B 项就是 productivity growth 的同义改写，与预判直接对应。 C) 张冠李戴 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 是作者本人的主张，不是传统观点对加薪基础的判断。 D) 张冠李戴 Mainstream economists insist that ... compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. 是主流经济学家的判断，且原文中"市场力量的无误判 断"是指工资水平的决定方式，不是加薪的依据。 关于美国过去50年左右的现实世界情况,我们了解到什么? A) 人们未能看到工资和生产率的相应增长。 B) 人们对贫富差距的扩大感到沮丧。 C) 人们目睹了共和党和民主党就减税问题展开的拉锯战。 D) 人们看到生产率与工人福祉之间的联系正在消失。

options.label: D
options.text: The unerring judgment of market forces.

questions.stem: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so? 问我们从原文得知的事实，原文必有对应陈述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?——主干是 What do we learn about things，三层介词短语 in the real world/in America/for the past 50 years or so 层层限定 things；六级长题干常用这种层层限定， 要逐层抓住主体（things=各种情况）。 50. What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so? A) People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity. B) People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots. C) People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts. D) People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. 在现实世界里，情况更复杂。工资受到雇主与工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直在胜出。 一个明显的证据是，自 1970 年前后以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距越来越大：生 产率已经翻了一倍多，而工资远远落在后面。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. ↔ People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity. the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth ↔ a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity A 项用 failed to see a corresponding increase 表达"生产率翻倍而工资落后"的整体含 义，与预判完全吻合。 B) 无中生有 原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资博弈，不是贫富分化 （haves and have-nots）；且原文未提任何人 disheartened（沮丧）。 C) 偷换概念 原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资双方的拉锯战，而非两党 的争斗；且原文未说民主党与共和党在减税上拉锯。 D) 过度推断 Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. 说的是"差距 扩大"，并未说"联系消失（link disappearing）"——差距大 ≠ 联系断；且 well-being （福祉）也比 wages 范围更大。

options.label: A
options.text: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.

options.label: B
options.text: People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots.

options.label: C
options.text: People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts.

options.label: D
options.text: People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.

questions.stem: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities? 问的是「鉴于职责，应当呈现什么」，是原文一句话可 以直接回答的事实，不含 infer/imply。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干是 What would we expect an editorial board…to exhibit，what 作 exhibit 的 宾语前置；in view of its important responsibilities 是介词短语作原因状语，可剥离。剥 离后等价于 We expect an editorial board to exhibit what?，结构平铺，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. 那么，你会希望期刊竭尽所能去建立一个多元化的编委会，从而反映各种各样的声音、经验 与身份。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 全文没有任何句子提到「洞察力」相关概念，Insight 是从职责一词主观联想出来的 属性。 B) 偷换概念 原文谈的是编辑的「身份多样性」而非「专业能力」；编辑工作虽要求专业，但全文没 有任何一句强调专业能力，Expertise 是属性偷换。 C) 无中生有 全文未出现「诚信／正直」相关讨论，Integrity 同样是从「重要职责」一词联想出的主 观属性。 D) ✓ 正确 diverse editorial board ↔Diversity 预判语义「多元」与 Diversity 完全同义，其它三项均无对应原文支撑，锁定 D。 51. What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities? A) Insight. B) Expertise. C) Integrity. D) Diversity. 我们从Nature Neuroscience上一项新研究的发现中了解到什么? A) 大多数顶级心理学和神经科学期刊反映了多样化的声音、经历和身份。 B) 大多数心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会确实影响着其领域发展的方向。 C) 心理学和神经科学领域最重要期刊的编委会由男性主导。 D) 顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑具有相关背景。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience? 问的是 研究本身陈述了什么，原文有直陈句，不需要跨段推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干 What do we learn from the findings…?，what 作 learn 的宾语前置；from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience 是 of 套 of 的多层介词结构，但只 是限定 findings 来源，对理解无障碍。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. 研究团队发现，顶级心理学与神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，且在美国工作——这种状 况可能正在放大该领域既有的性别不平等，并影响着哪些研究得以发表。 52. What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience? A) The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities. B) The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes. C) The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male- dominated. D) The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities 是 P1 中作者「期望」的状 态，而 P2 恰恰指出现实并非如此——选项把「期待」当成「现实」，方向完全反了。 B) 答非所问 do influence the direction their field takes 借用 influencing the direction that a field takes，但那是 P1 描述「编辑职责」的总论，不是 P2 的「研究发现」；题干问 findings of a new study，本选项答的是 P1 的背景，与 52 题问的范围错位。 C) ✓ 正确 the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male ↔ The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated. top psychology and neuroscience journals ↔ the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience 「顶级=最重要」「以男为主=男性主导」两组同义替换都成立，C 是定位句的精确同义 复述。 D) 无中生有 全文没有任何句子谈及编辑的「相关背景／资质」是否充足；P2 谈的是性别和国籍分 布，不是专业相关性，have relevant backgrounds 凭空冒出。 关于心理学期刊编辑的性别差异,作者强调了什么事实? A) 有相当多的女性编辑也作为有影响力的心理学研究者脱颖而出。 B) 女性编辑的数量与从事心理学研究的女性数量根本不成比例。 C) 女性编辑的比例在高级职位上越来越低。 D) 很少有女性编辑能够晋升到高级职位。

options.label: A
options.text: The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities.

options.label: B
options.text: The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes.

options.label: C
options.text: The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male- dominated.

options.label: D
options.text: The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.

questions.stem: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals? 问的是「作者强调了什么事实」，原文有一句直接陈述，属细节而非 主旨。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干 What fact does the author highlight…?；concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals 是 concerning 引导的介词短语作 highlight 的范围状 语，限定话题。结构平铺，无陷阱。 53. What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals? A) There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers. B) The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research. C) The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels. D) There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. 至关重要的是，女性编辑的占比显著低于心理学领域整体女性研究者的占比。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 原文只对比「女编辑占比」与「女研究者占比」，并未说有「兼任出色研究者的女编 辑」；distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers 是凭空添加 的属性。 B) ✓ 正确 the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers ↔ The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research. the overall proportion of women psychology researchers ↔ that of women engaged in psychology research 唯一刻画「女编辑占比 vs 女研究者占比」这一比例对照的选项是 B；其它选项要么换了 对比对象，要么换了讨论范围。 C) 过度推断 The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels. 把原文 「各级别男编辑都更多」的事实曲解为「越往高级越少」的递进趋势；原文 There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority 只说「每一 级都更多」，并没有给出「越往上越严重」的递进关系。 D) 偷换概念 原文没有讨论「女编辑能否升迁」这一职业流动问题；few female editors who could move up to senior positions 把性别比例话题换成升迁话题，方向错位。 从新研究团队基于其发现得出的结论中,我们可以推断出什么? A) 女性的观点在顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会中代表性不足。 B) 顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的男性编辑往往对其女性同事存在偏见。 C) 男性研究者在编委会中有足够的代表性来确保他们的论文发表。 D) 女性编辑必须努力争取才能让女性的研究文章在学术期刊上发表。 54. What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings? A) Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals. B) Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues. C) Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications. D) Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.

options.label: A
options.text: There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers.

options.label: B
options.text: The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.

options.label: C
options.text: The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels.

options.label: D
options.text: There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings? 含明确的 infer 标志词，正确答案是定位句的一步同义延伸，而非 原文逐字表述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干 What can we infer from the conclusion…?；drawn by the team of the new study 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 conclusion；on the basis of their findings 是介 词短语状语，说明结论的依据。三层修饰仅在定位 conclusion 这个核心名词，不影响主干 理解，但基础薄弱的同学要看清 from 后面真正的对象是 conclusion 而不是 team。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience." 基于研究结果，研究团队总结道：「在最受认可的心理学与神经科学学术期刊的编辑岗位 上，男性的想法、价值观与决策偏见被过度代表。」

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented ↔ Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals. the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience ↔the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals 在「男过度代表」基础上仅走一步就到「女代表不足」，A 是唯一这样做的；其它选项 要么走第二步（偏见、歧视），要么换了话题。 B) 过度推断 原文 decision-making biases of men 指的是「决策中的偏见模式被过度呈现」这一统 计事实；be biased against their female colleagues 则把它推到「男编辑刻意歧视女 同事」的人际行为层面，多走了一步。 C) 答非所问 题干问「能推断出什么」，ensure their publications 谈的是「男编辑的发表得到保 障」，原文没有任何句子谈论这种保障机制；且本研究的论调是批评不平等而非赞颂男 性发表优势，与原文立场相反。 D) 无中生有 原文从未谈论女编辑为发表女性研究而「斗争」，struggle to get women's research articles published 是凭空虚构出来的情节。 作者建议我们做什么,而不是简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统? A) 在男性和女性编辑之间取得平衡。 B) 增加女性在高级职位上的任职。 C) 扩大女性学者的群体。 D) 实施全面的结构性改革。

options.label: A
options.text: Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals.

options.label: B
options.text: Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues.

options.label: C
options.text: Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications.

options.label: D
options.text: Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.

questions.stem: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition? 问作者明确建议什么，原文有 Rather than… we should… 的直陈句，是细节题而非主旨题。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干 What does the author suggest we do，what 作 do 的宾语前置；instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition 是 instead of 引导的动 名词介词短语，作状语，表达「与其…不如…」的对比关系。看清 instead of 后面是「要被 否定的旧做法」，suggest we do 后面才是「要肯定的新做法」，二者不可弄反。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. 实际上，是结构性的原因让女性在科学界处于不利地位。例如，女性薪资更低、育儿负担更 重，这会导致她们论文与基金更少——而这些恰恰是期刊在选拔编辑时所看重的。与其简单 地把编委会的不平等推给传统，不如主动去拆除这些既有的壁垒。 55. What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition? A) Strike a balance between male and female editors. B) Increase women's employment in senior positions. C) Enlarge the body of female academics. D) Implement overall structural reforms.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 以偏概全 Strike a balance between male and female editors 只触及「编辑性别比例」这一表 层结果，与作者主张的「拆除导致不平等的结构性原因」相比，停留在症状而非根因； 原文反对的就是「只盯比例不动结构」的浅层对策。 B) 答非所问 Increase women's employment in senior positions 借的是 P6 「初级岗位也男性偏 多」这一对照性数据；但 P6 是作者用来「驳斥传统论」的论据，并非建议；55 题问的 是「P7 作者建议什么」。 C) 与原文相反 原文 This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. 已明确否定 「女学者太少」是问题；Enlarge the body of female academics 恰恰反过来主张「扩 充女学者队伍」，方向完全相反。 D) ✓ 正确 actively breaking down these existing barriers ↔Implement overall structural reforms. structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science ↔structural reforms 把「主动拆除结构性壁垒」概括为「实施整体结构性改革」，是 D 与原文唯一吻合的 同义改写；其它选项要么停留在「男女比例」「升迁」等局部对策，要么误把原因当 对策。

options.label: A
options.text: Strike a balance between male and female editors.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase women's employment in senior positions.

options.label: C
options.text: Enlarge the body of female academics.

P1 One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.

P2 The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.

P3 Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.

P4 This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P5 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.

P6 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.

P7 Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.

P8 The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.

P9 Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.

P10 The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.

P11 It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.

P12 In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.

P13 A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote(矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.

P1 Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.

P2 Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.

P3 Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P4 The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.

P5 Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."

P6 Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.

P7 This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.

P8 A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.

writing.model: As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject. Just as a towering building cannot stand firm without a solid foundation, no student can reach academic heights unless the fundamentals are first laid down. The basics are not the trivial part of learning; they are the very ground on which deeper understanding is built. In my own experience, this truth was made vivid when I began studying programming. At first I was eager to write fancy applications and skipped the elementary concepts of variables and loops. As a result, whenever a bug appeared, I had no idea where to look, and my code collapsed completely. It follows that students should never underestimate the value of the basics. Rather than rushing toward complicated tasks, we ought to devote patient effort to consolidating the fundamentals first. Only by standing on such firm ground can we climb steadily toward true mastery of any subject.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 养老(作主语)+受到关注(谓语)（主语策略：原句主语） 核心是养老受到普遍关注，主语"养老"=elderly care，谓语"受到普遍关注"用被动 has drawn / receives widespread attention，宾语是 attention。"在中国""随着老龄化社会的到来"都是背景 状语，不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两层背景降级为介词短语 "在中国"降为介词短语 In China 置句首；随着老龄化社会的到来降为 with the arrival of an aging society（with + 名词短语），不另起一句、不用 and 平铺。两个状语都挂在主干前，主干 只保留"养老受到关注"。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 语态 "养老受到关注"是"养老"承受"关注"这个动作，用被动更自然：elderly care has drawn widespread attention（draw 主动表"引起"亦可），切忌写成 elderly care pays attention 这种 主客颠倒。 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时 / 现在完成时；本句陈述当下普遍状态，用 has drawn（强调已成普遍 现象）或 receives 均可。 冠词与单复数 "老龄化社会"泛指一类社会，用不定冠词 an aging society；elderly care 为不可数抽象概念，不 加 -s、不加冠词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In China, with the arrival of an aging society, elderly care has drawn widespread attention. 2. 人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: What引导的主语从句作真正话题（主语策略：形式主语it） 人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式核心是"人们最常谈论的（话题）是 X"。可用 What people talk about most is… 直接以 what 从句作主语；也可写 The most discussed topic is…。 谓语是系动词 is，表语是"该采取什么养老模式"这个间接问句。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 宾语从句嵌入表语 "应当采取什么样的养老模式"作表语，降级为名词性从句 what model of elderly care should be adopted（间接疑问，疑问词 what + 陈述语序）。"应当采取"用 should be adopted 表"应被采 取"，把"采取"的对象"模式"提作从句主语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 主句陈述当下普遍现象，用一般现在时 is，回指全篇基调。 语态 "应当采取"的逻辑承受者是"模式"，从句用被动 should be adopted，比补一个泛泛主语 we should adopt 更客观，契合说明文语体。 单复数与搭配 "养老模式"此处泛指某一种待选模式，用单数 model；搭配用 model of elderly care 或 elderly- care model，固定沿用 glossary 译法。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: What people talk about most is what model of elderly care should be adopted. 3. 多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Most people(主)+believe(谓)+that从句(宾)（主语策略：原句主语） 多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化主语"多数人"=Most people，谓语"认为"=believe / hold，宾 语是 that 引导的宾语从句"养老模式需要多元化"。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 本就是主从句无需再降级 "养老模式需要多元化"作 that 从句，主语 the elderly-care model，谓语 needs to be，表语 diversified（"多元化"用形容词/过去分词表状态）。结构本就清晰，只需把"多元化"这个动词性中 文词转成 be diversified 即可。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "多数人认为"是当下普遍看法，主句与从句都用一般现在时，回指全篇基调。 主谓一致 Most people 为复数，谓语用 believe（不加 -s）；从句主语 the model 为单数第三人称，谓语 needs 要加 -s，两处别混。 搭配 "需要多元化"=needs to be diversified（need to do）；"多元"亦可名词化为 a diversity of models，但与 glossary 单数 model 表述需协调，此处取 be diversified 更省心。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Most people believe that the elderly-care model needs to be diversified. 4. 可以通过政府引导和社会参与，建立更多更好的养老服务机构，改进社区服务中心，鼓励居 家自助养老，还可以推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: We(补)+can(谓)+四个并列动作(宾/不定式)（主语策略：补主语） 本句中文无主语，是"可以做哪些事"的措施罗列。补一个泛指主语 We，谓语用 can，后接四个并 列的措施动词：建立更多更好的养老服务机构build…、改进社区服务中心improve…、鼓励居家自 助养老encourage…、推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式promote…。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 通过…降为by短语，四措施并列 通过政府引导和社会参与降级为方式状语 through governmental guidance and social participation（through + 名词，不译成从句）；其后"建立""改进""鼓励""推行"四个动作并列作 can 的并列谓语，用逗号 + and 连接最后一项：build…, improve…, encourage…, and promote…，结构整齐不流水。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态语态 讲"可以采取的做法"，用 We can + 动词原形（一般现在时情态结构）；若想更客观可整体转被 动：…can be established and improved，主语换成措施对象。 单复数 "更多更好的养老服务机构"是复数 more and better elderly-care institutions（-s）；"社区服务 中心"泛指多个，用复数 community service centers。可数名词逐个定数。 搭配与并列对齐 四个动词搭配各就位：build/establish institutions、improve centers、encourage self- supported home-based care、promote a combination of…；四项词性须对齐（都用动词原 形），不可一项用动词、一项突然换成名词。 用词统一 "居家自助养老""家庭养老与社会养老相结合"沿用 glossary 既定译法 self-supported home- based elderly care、a combination of family-based and society-based elderly care，全篇一 致。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Through governmental guidance and social participation, we can build more and better elderly-care institutions, improve community service centers, encourage self- supported home-based elderly care, and promote a combination of family-based and society-based elderly care. 5. 随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加，养老设施将不断升级，服务质量逐步改 进，老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适、健康快乐。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 三个并列主谓预测未来（主语策略：原句主语） 本句主干是三组"什么将怎样"的并列分句：养老设施将不断升级facilities will be upgraded、服务 质量逐步改进service quality will improve、老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适\、健康快乐the elderly will live more conveniently…。"随着……投入的持续增加"是背景状语，不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 随着…降为with短语，结果分句并列 随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加降级为 with the continuous increase in government and social investment in elderly-care services（with + 名词短语）；三组结果分 句并列作主干，末项"方便舒适、健康快乐"可用副词 more conveniently and comfortably, healthily and happily 修饰"生活/活着"。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 本句是全篇唯一偏离基调处："将不断升级""将会更加"是对未来的预测，三个分句统一用一般将来 时 will be upgraded / will improve / will live，与前四句的一般现在时区分。 语态 "养老设施将升级"中设施是被升级的承受者，用被动 will be upgraded；"服务质量改进"可用 improve 的不及物主动 will improve（质量自身变好），两者各按逻辑定。 单复数与冠词 "养老设施"复数 facilities；"老年人"用 the elderly（the + 形容词表一类人，作复数）或 elderly people，谓语相应用复数 will live。 搭配 "对……的投入"=investment in…（介词 in，不是 to）；"持续增加"=continuous increase / continuously increase。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the continuous increase in government and social investment in elderly-care services, elderly-care facilities will be steadily upgraded, service quality will gradually improve, and the elderly will live a more convenient, comfortable, healthy and happy life. 英语六级 2023年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
